waypoints.title: MARQUEE TRAVERSAL INVARIANT (operator 2026-09-22): a notification must ALWAYS scroll offscreen -> onscreen -> offscreen at least once; never 'just appear', never vanish, never tear visually or temporally. The s91 ring fails the at-least-once half: pendingText is rebuilt from the model on every count change, so an item that arrives and expires before the next boundary never shows. Design: a QUEUE keyed by notification id (the model's IdRole / index key) — an arrival is appended with shown=false; at a boundary the next ring is [every queued item with shown=false] (expired or not), which then scrolls exactly once; an item still in the model after its rotation may be re-queued (it keeps cycling while active); an item removed from the model finishes its current rotation and is dropped at the boundary; the ring NEVER changes mid-rotation. Pure functions in marquee-body.js (ringNext(queue, modelIds) -> {ring, queue}) so the headless harness proves the invariant on synthetic arrival/expiry sequences

waypoints.title: THE MATRIX AS A VIEWPORT (operator 2026-09-22): the 5x8 cell is a WINDOW over a taller raster, scrolled vertically — how a single-row board shows anything taller than its LEDs. One mechanism, three payloads: (a) ICONS — the app icon rasterised at runtime in QML (an Image via Qt's icon provider, drawn into a hidden Canvas, getImageData, coverage-threshold or ordered-dither to column bytes — matrix_glyph's rule in JS) as a 16- or 32-row bitmap scrolled vertically through the 8-row window while the text scrolls horizontally; (b) UNICODE / UNIFONT — 8x16 glyphs (CJK, non-Latin) via W30's font compiler emitting a 16-row table, shown by the same vertical scroll or by a 2:1 downsample when legible; (c) any oversized bitmap (a QR code, a logo). This retires the icons-are-residue verdict (s96/W46)

Relations: the raster's lit dots are the lit token; no colour from the icon (the hue gate of §5a would apply if wanted, later).

waypoints.title: SPARKLINES ON THE MATRIX (operator 2026-09-22). A DATA RUN: a series of values -> column heights on the 8 rows (one column per sample, the newest at the right), scrolling like text or pinned at the board's end; the one thing a segment display cannot do and a matrix can. Sources: a job's percentage over time (W46's progress bar is the degenerate one-sample case), Plasma's systemmonitor sensors (CPU, net, temperature — org.kde.ksysguard.sensors / Plasma's SensorDataModel in Plasma 6: measure the QML import), the notification arrival rate itself. Rendering: a run type 'series' in the ring (values[], min/max, lit column height = round(v/max*rows)); optional baseline row; bold = fuller dots; colour via the §5a hue gate (a sensor's colour is a sender colour). Settings: which sensors, samples per column

waypoints.title: REQUIREMENTS AS REGO (operator: OPA/Rego is a standardized, machine-parseable, machine-actionable spec format; the chk() arms overwhelm an LLM with cognitive load). Split every check into MEASUREMENT and POLICY: a check's --json mode emits what it measured (the population, per-item facts, SKIPs as withheld) and nothing else; policy/<check>.rego declares the requirement as deny/withheld sets over that JSON (luthen's shape: D0 vacuity guard first - an empty population is a deny; withheld separate from deny); policy/<check>_test.rego carries the refuse/admit pair per rule (this REPLACES the chk() falsifiability arms, which shrink to 'the measurement can see'); scripts/opa_gate.py runs opa eval per check and maps deny/withheld to exit 1/3; worklist warrants cite the rego rule. opa is at /usr/bin/opa. First: check_qml_lint (newest, smallest) as the pilot, then check_marquee_body's ring scenarios (already JSON), then the rest by sweep.

waypoints.title: HOVER-PAUSE INDICATOR (operator: 'a visual indicator for when hover is active. Perhaps a pulsing outline? the outermost pips of the matrix fading in and out - something clear, active, responsive, and will get someone to move the damn mouse'). While rotation.paused (hover-pause holding the board): MatrixField draws its outermost ring of pips (top row, bottom row, first and last columns) at a separate opacity that a SequentialAnimation pulses between the ghost alpha and the lit alpha (~0.8 s period, Easing.InOutSine); nothing else on the board changes, the run resumes when the pointer leaves. Colour: the ring pulses toward the lit token (not fg_act - this is attention, not alarm; W46's urgency owns hot). Harness: check_marquee_live --hovered samples a new root property boardPaused plus the field's ringOpacity; policy rule L7: while paused the ring opacity CHANGES across samples (a pulse), and while not paused it equals the ghost alpha. Settings: none new - the pulse belongs to hoverPause.
